topic: Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer (ACE) exam preparation - Google Cloud's associate certification for deploying applications, monitoring operations, and managing enterprise solutions on Google Cloud using the Console and the gcloud CLI
cert_name: Google Cloud Certified - Associate Cloud Engineer
exam_format: Approximately 50-60 multiple-choice and multiple-select questions, 120 minutes, taken online-proctored or at a test center. Passing is not published as a fixed number but is commonly cited around 70%; Google does NOT publish the official passing score or official per-domain percentage weightings, so the domain weights in this course are editorial estimates that reflect the emphasis of Google's official ACE exam guide, not Google's official figures. Exam fee is approximately USD 125 plus tax and varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Google Cloud pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and scenario-based questions; the exam tests choosing the correct Google Cloud action/service/gcloud command for a described situation
audience: Cloud engineers, sysadmins, developers, and IT professionals with some hands-on Google Cloud experience who deploy and operate workloads on GCP. Recommended 6+ months of hands-on Google Cloud use. A strong associate-level foundation and a companion to the Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer and Generative AI Leader courses in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment
domains.notes: The foundation: the resource hierarchy (organization, folders, projects) and creating/managing projects and billing. Enabling APIs, setting up billing accounts, budgets and alerts, and quotas. Installing and configuring the Cloud SDK and gcloud CLI, Cloud Shell, and configurations/contexts. Choosing the correct project/billing/hierarchy setup for a described organizational requirement.

domains.name: Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution
domains.notes: Choosing and sizing the right products for a workload: compute options (Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run, App Engine, Cloud Functions) and when to use each; storage and database selection (Cloud Storage classes, Persistent Disk, Filestore, Cloud SQL, Spanner, Bigtable, Firestore, BigQuery); and networking design (VPC, subnets, IP ranges). Using the Pricing Calculator to estimate cost. Selecting the MOST appropriate, cost-effective service and configuration for a described scenario is the recurring skill.

domains.name: Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution
domains.notes: The heaviest domain: deploying Compute Engine VMs (machine types, images, startup scripts, snapshots, instance templates, managed instance groups, autoscaling); deploying GKE clusters and workloads (nodes, node pools, kubectl basics); deploying serverless (Cloud Run, App Engine, Cloud Functions); and data solutions (Cloud SQL, BigQuery jobs, Pub/Sub, Dataproc/Dataflow at a deploy level). Infrastructure-as-code with Deployment Manager / Terraform basics and gcloud/Console/Cloud Shell workflows. Choosing the right deployment approach and commands for a described requirement.

domains.name: Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution
domains.notes: Day-2 operations: managing Compute Engine (start/stop/resize, disks, snapshots, images), GKE (scaling, rolling updates), and storage/databases (lifecycle policies, backups, read replicas). Monitoring and logging with Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging (metrics, dashboards, alerting policies, uptime checks, log sinks/exports) and Error Reporting/Trace. Managing costs and viewing billing reports. Choosing the correct operational action or observability tool for a described problem.

domains.name: Configuring Access and Security
domains.notes: Cloud IAM: roles (basic, predefined, custom), members/principals, service accounts and keys, and the principle of least privilege. Assigning roles at the right resource-hierarchy level, managing service-account impersonation, and IAM conditions. Viewing audit logs and basic security controls (org policies at an awareness level). Choosing the correct IAM role, service account, or access configuration for a described least-privilege requirement.

extra_guidance: Google Cloud Associate Cloud Engineer (ACE) is one of the highest-volume cloud certifications and the associate-level GCP entry point, complementing the Professional Machine Learning Engineer and Generative AI Leader courses already in this catalog. CRITICAL accuracy note: Google does NOT publish official per-domain percentage weightings or the passing score for the ACE exam, so present the domain NAMES exactly as they appear in Google's official exam guide (Setting Up a Cloud Solution Environment; Planning and Configuring a Cloud Solution; Deploying and Implementing a Cloud Solution; Ensuring Successful Operation of a Cloud Solution; Configuring Access and Security) but mark the weights as editorial estimates (leading '~'), never as Google's official figures - state this where weights appear. This is a HANDS-ON, tool-driven exam: the real skill is choosing the correct Google Cloud service AND the correct gcloud/Console/Cloud Shell action for a described scenario, so practice questions MUST be scenario-based with 'BEST / MOST cost-effective / correct next step' framing and MUST use exact GCP terminology and gcloud command patterns (gcloud compute instances create, gcloud container clusters, gsutil/gcloud storage, gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding, instance templates + managed instance groups, IAM predefined vs custom roles, VPC subnets). Cover the classic decision pairs relentlessly: Compute Engine vs GKE vs Cloud Run vs App Engine vs Cloud Functions; Cloud SQL vs Spanner vs Bigtable vs Firestore vs BigQuery; Standard vs Nearline vs Coldline vs Archive storage classes; basic vs predefined vs custom IAM roles; Deployment Manager vs Terraform. Labs are read-and-understand gcloud/Console walkthroughs (create a VM and a managed instance group, deploy to Cloud Run and GKE, set an IAM binding on a service account, create a budget alert, set up a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy), not deep coding. Frame the credential honestly as 'exam-focused preparation' - never promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in any form (Udemy compliance). Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a time-management strategy for the ~50-60 question, 120-minute format. Do NOT invent Google's official passing score or exact fee; present the fee as approximate (~USD 125) and advise verifying current Google Cloud pricing. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Azure) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
